questions.q: A heavy ball of mass $M$ is suspended from the ceiling of a car by a light string of mass $m\left(m ≪ M\right) .$ When the car is at rest, the speed of transverse waves in the string is $60\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1} .$ When the car has acceleration $a,$ the wave-speed increases to $60.5\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1} .$ The value of $a,$ in terms of gravitational acceleration $g,$ is closed to
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For standing car,& $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{μ}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{Mg}{μ}}$



For accelerating car,

$υ′ = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sqrt{{( Mg )}^{2} + {( Ma )}^{2}}}{\mu}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{60.5}{60} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sqrt{{( Mg )}^{2} + {( Ma )}^{2}}}{Mg}}$

$⇒ {\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{120}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{{( Mg )}^{2} + {( Ma )}^{2}}}{Mg}$

$⇒ 1 + \dfrac{2}{120} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{a^{2}}{g^{2}}}$

$\approx \dfrac{2}{120} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{a^{2}}{g^{2}}$

$∴ a = g\sqrt{\dfrac{4}{120}} = \dfrac{g}{\sqrt{30}} \approx \dfrac{g}{5}$

questions.q: A sinusoidal wave of wavelength 7.5 cm travels a distance of 1.2 cm along the x -direction in 0.3 sec. The crest $P$ is at $x=0$ at $t=0 \mathrm\sec$ and maximum displacement of the wave is 2 cm. Which equation correctly represents this wave ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{v}=\frac{\text { distance }}{\text { time }} \\ & \mathrm{v}=\frac{12}{0.3}=4 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \mathrm{k}=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}=\frac{2 \pi}{7.5}=\frac{4 \pi}{15}=0.83 \\ & \mathrm{v}=\frac{\omega}{\mathrm{k}} \Rightarrow \omega=\mathrm{vk}=4 \times \frac{4 \pi}{15}=3.35
\end{aligned}$
So $y=A \cos (k x-\omega t)$

questions.q: A closed organ pipe has a fundamental frequency of $1.5kHz$. The number of overtones that can be distinctly heard by a person with this organ pipe will be~$(Assume that the highest frequency a person can hear is $20,000Hz$).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a& closed organ pipe, the resonate frequency(harmonics) is an odd multiple of the& fundamental frequency.

Therefore,& \left(2n - 1\right){f}_{0} \le 20000Hz$,~where~$n = 1, 2, 3 . . .$

${f}_{0} = 1 . 5kHz ⇒$~fundamental frequency

Then,~$n = 7$

The total number of overtones~that can be heard~is $6$.~(${2}^{nd}$~harmonic to~${7}^{th}$ \text{ and } harmonic. )

$

questions.q: A tuning fork $A$ of unknown frequency produces $5beatss^{- 1}$~with a fork of known frequency $340$ Hz. When fork $A$ is filed, the beat frequency decreases to $2beatss^{- 1}$. What is the frequency of fork $A$ ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initially beat frequency $= 5Hz$

so, ${ρ}_{A} = 340 \pm 5 = 345Hz,$~or $335$ Hz~

after filing frequency increases slightly so, new value of frequency of $A > {ρ}_{A}$

Now, beat frequency $= 2Hz$

$⇒$ new ${ρ}_{A} = 340 \pm 2 = 342Hz,$~or $338$ Hz

hence, original frequency of $A$ is ${ρ}_{A} = 335Hz$

questions.q: A string $2.0m$ long and fixed at its ends is driven by a $240$ Hz vibrator. The string vibrates in its third harmonic mode. The speed of the wave and its fundamental frequency is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a string fixed at both the ends,
$f = \dfrac{n}{2L}v$
For third harmonic, $240 = \dfrac{3}{2 ( 2 )}v$
$⇒ v = \dfrac{240 \times 4}{3}$
$= 320ms^{- 1}$
Fundamental frequency ${f}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{2L}v$
$= \dfrac{1}{4} \times 320 = 80Hz$

questions.q: In the resonance experiment, two air columns (closed at one end) of 100 cm and 120 cm long, give 15 beats per second when each one is sounding in the respective fundamental modes. The velocity of sound in the air column is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Fundamental frequency in close/organ pipe
$\begin{aligned} & (\mathrm{f})=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \ell} \\ & \mathrm{f}_1=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \ell_1} & \mathrm{f}_2=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \ell_2}\end{aligned}$
Beat $= \left(\mathrm{f}}_{1}- \mathrm{f}}_{2}\right)=$\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4}\left(\frac{1}{\ell_1}-\frac{1}{\ell_2}\right)
$\begin{aligned} \text{ and } 15=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4} \left(\frac{1}{1}-\frac{1}{1.2}\right)\\ \text{ and } \mathrm{v}=\left(\frac{15 \times 4 \times 1.2}{0.2}\right)=60 \times6=360 \mathrm{~m}/ \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Sound travels in a mixture of two moles of helium and $n$ moles of hydrogen. If rms speed of gas molecules in the mixture is $\sqrt{2}$ times the speed of sound, then the value of $n$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Speed of sound in a gas is given by,& ${v}_{s} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gammaRT}{M}}$

The formula for RMS speed is,~${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

It is given that~${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{2}{v}_{s}$

$⇒ \dfrac{vs}{vrms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{γ}{3}} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \dfrac{γ}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \gamma = \dfrac{3}{2}$

For~$\gamma$~of mixture,

${γ}_{mix} = \dfrac{CP, mix}{CV, mix} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2{C}_{P, H} + n{C}_{P, He}}{2 + n}}{2{C}_{V, H} + n{C}_{V, He}2 + n}$

Since~Hydrogen is a diatomic gas,~${C}_{V, H} = \dfrac{5}{2}R, {C}_{P, H} = \dfrac{7}{2}R$~and Helium is monatomic gas,~${C}_{V, He} = \dfrac{3}{2}R, {C}_{P, He} = \dfrac{5}{2}R$. Therefore,

${γ}_{mix} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2{C}_{P, H} + n{C}_{P, He}}{2 + n}}{2{C}_{V, H} + n{C}_{V, He}2 + n} ⇒ \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{7}{2}R + n \times \dfrac{5}{2}R}{2 \times \dfrac{5}{2}R + n \times \dfrac{3}{2}R}$

$⇒ n = 2$

questions.q: Two harmonic waves moving in the same direction superimpose to form a wave $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{a} \cos (1.5 \mathrm{t}) \cos (50.5 \mathrm{t})$ where $t$ is in seconds. Find the period with which they beat (close to nearest integer)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given equation can be written as
$\mathrm{x}=\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2} \cos [1.5+50.5] \mathrm{t}+\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2} \cos [50.5-1.5]$
$x=\frac{a}{2} \cos [52 t]+\frac{a}{2} \cos [49 t]$
Here, $2 \pi \mathrm{f}_1 \ \text{ and } 2 \pi \mathrm{f}_2=49$
$\mathrm{f}_1=\frac{52}{2 \pi}, \mathrm{f}_2=\frac{49}{2 \pi}$
$\therefore \mathrm{f}_{\text {Bat }}=\mathrm{f}_1-\mathrm{f}_2=\frac{3}{2 \pi} \mathrm{~Hz}$
$\therefore \mathrm{T}_{\text {Beat }}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{\text {Beat }}}=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \mathrm\sec$
$=2.09 \mathrm\sec \approx 2 \mathrm\sec$

questions.q: A travelling harmonic wave is represented by the equation $y\left(x, t\right) = {10}^{- 3}\sin \left(50t + 2x\right)\text{,}$ where $x$ and $y$ are in meter and $t$ is in seconds. Which of the following is a correct statement about the wave?
options: The wave is propagating along the positive $x$ -axis with speed $25ms^{- 1}$
The wave is propagating along the positive $x$ -axis with speed $100ms^{- 1}$
The wave is propagating along the negative $x$ -axis with speed $25ms^{- 1}$
The wave is propagating along the negative $x$ -axis with speed $100ms^{- 1}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given wave equation,& $y \left(x, t\right) = {10}^{- 3}\sin \left($50t + 2x\right)$

This equation is similar to the equation of wave travelling along the negative~$x$-axis which is given by

$y \left($x, t\right) = Asin \left(\omegat +$kx\right)$

After comparing, Angular frequency~\omega =$50s^{- 1}$

Wave number~$k = 2m^{- 1}$

The wave velocity,~$v = $\dfrac{ω}{k} = \dfrac{50}{2} =$25ms^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: A closed organ and an open organ tube are filled by two different gases having same bulk modulus but different densities $\rho_1$ and $\rho_{2^{\prime}}$, respectively. The frequency of $9^{\text {th }}$ harmonic of closed tube is identical with $4^{\text {th }}$ harmonic of open tube. If the length of the closed tube is 10 cm and the density ratio of the gases is $\rho_1: \rho_2=1: 16$, then the length of the open tube is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 9^{\text {th }} \text { harmonic of closed pipe }=\frac{9 \mathrm{~V}_1}{4 \ell_1} \\ & 4^{\text {th }} \text { harmonic of open pipe }=\frac{2 \mathrm{~V}_2}{\ell_2} \\ & \therefore \frac{9 \mathrm{~V}_1}{4 \ell_1}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~V}_2}{\ell_2} \\ & \therefore \frac{9}{4 \ell_1} \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{~B}}{\rho_1}}=\frac{2}{\ell_2} \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{~B}}{\rho_2}} \Rightarrow \frac{\ell_2}{\ell_1}=\frac{8}{9} \sqrt{\frac{\rho_1}{\rho_2}} \\ & \ell_2=\ell_1 \times \frac{8}{9} \times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{20}{9} \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An organ pipe $40$ cm long is open at both ends. The speed of sound in air is $360ms^{- 1}$. The frequency of the second harmonic is _________Hz .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula for the frequency in an open organ pipe is&

$f = \dfrac{nv}{2L}$

Since, it is a second harmonic,~$n = 2$

The frequency of the second harmonic becomes~$f = \dfrac{2v}{2L} = \dfrac{v}{L}$

The data given is~

$L = 0 . 4mv = 360ms^{- 1}$

Substituting the values in the frequency formula

$f = \dfrac{360ms^{- 1}}{0 . 4m} = 900Hz$

questions.q: A point source is emitting sound waves of intensity $16 \times {10}^{- 8}Wm^{- 2}$ at the origin. The difference in intensity (magnitude only) at two points located at a distances of $2m$ and $4m$ from the origin respectively will be ________\times {10}^{- 8}Wm^{- 2}.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Intensity for a point source varies as $I ∝ \dfrac{1}{r2}$.

Intensity at a distance of $2m$, ${I}_{2} = 16 \times {10}^{- 8} \times \dfrac{1}{22} = 4 \times {10}^{- 8}Wm^{- 2}$

Similarly, intensity at a distance of $4m$, ${I}_{4} = 16 \times {10}^{- 8} \times \dfrac{1}{42} = 1 \times {10}^{- 8}Wm^{- 2}$

Required difference, ${I}_{2} - {I}_{4} = 3 \times {10}^{- 8}Wm^{- 2}$

questions.q: A set of $20$ tuning forks is arranged in a series of increasing frequencies. If each fork gives $4$ beats with respect to the preceding fork and the frequency of the last fork is twice the frequency of the first, then the frequency of last fork is _____~$Hz$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Each fork produces $4$~beats per second with the previous means each fork has frequency $4$ Hz more than the previous.

Using relation,~${f}_{last} = {f}_{first} + \left(N - 1\right)x$, here,~$N$~is~the number of tuning fork in series and~$x$~is~beat frequency between two successive forks.

$2{f}_{0} = {f}_{0} + \left(20 - 1\right)4$

$⇒ 2{f}_{0} = {f}_{0} + 76 ⇒ {f}_{0} = 76Hz$

Frequency of last tuning fork is~$152$ Hz.

questions.q: The displacement equations of two interfering waves are given by& ${y}_{1} = 10\sin \left(\omegat + \dfrac{π}{3}\right)cm$,~${y}_{2} = 5\left[\sin \left(\omegat\right) + \sqrt{3}cos\omegat\right]cm$~respectively. The amplitude of the resultant wave is _____~$cm$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Displacement equation of second wave can be written as,${y}_{2} = 5\left(sin\omegat + \sqrt{3}cos\omegat\right) = 10\left(sin\omegat \times \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2} \times cos\omegat\right) = 10 \left($sin\omegat \$timescos\dfrac{π}{3} +++sin\dfrac{π}{3} \timescos\omegat\right)

$= 10\sin \left(\omegat + \dfrac{π}{3}\right)$

As we can see, the phase difference between the waves is $0$. Therefore, resultant amplitude will be sum of the amplitudes of the waves.

So $A = {A}_{1} + {A}_{2} = 10cm + 10cm = 20cm$

$
